subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron runs get an explicit `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue relying on per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This chooses a public config surface and security boundary for scheduled automation, including how cron message delivery interacts with tool authorization and existing policy layers.

options.title: Add explicit cron policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence over or under per-job `toolsAllow`, and test message-tool denial for announce, none, and webhook modes.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron isolated sessions as sharing `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing config surface but coupling two session classes with different delivery semantics.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Document per-job `toolsAllow` as the supported restriction path and avoid a global cron config knob, accepting that operators must configure each cron job.

recommendation.title: Add explicit cron policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence over or under per-job `toolsAllow`, and test message-tool denial for announce, none, and webhook modes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the centralized capability-profile policy path and previously reviewed this exact cron policy gap.
